boarding.title: Boarding (10 min call)
boarding.rule1: Meet Jump Master at loading area, fully geared up
boarding.rule2: Line up with your freefall group

inAircraft.title: In the aircraft
inAircraft.rule1: Everyone buckled with helmet on until 1500 ft
inAircraft.rule4: Red light = open door, Green = jump!

landingPattern.title: Landing Pattern
landingPattern.rule1: Downwind always runs straight south or north, parallel to the runway
landingPattern.rule2: Max 90° turn for landing north or south
landingPattern.rule3: Don't cross the runway below 300 ft (in extension: 1000 ft)
landingPattern.rule4: Max deployment altitude: 5000 ft (shared airspace with Torp)

outlanding.title: Outlanding
outlanding.rule1: Report via BurbleMe so we know where you are
outlanding.rule2: Follow tractor tracks, trample as little as possible! (500 NOK fine)
outlanding.rule3: Watch out for the cows in the north end – they can be dangerous!
outlanding.rule4: Report to HFL as soon as you're back

aircraft.title: Twin Otter –
aircraft.intro: We are very proud of our aircraft – LN-JMP – a newly overhauled Twin Otter with room for 20 jumpers. The aircraft type is DHC6-200, and JMP was produced at the De Havilland factory in Canada in 1968.
aircraft.history: JMP came to Jarlsberg in 2006 and is now owned by Hoppfly AS, where TøFSK has 10% and the main owner is Per Kølner.
aircraft.renovation: Before the 2016 season, JMP was completely renovated for over 10 million NOK, with new instruments, new paint, and not least new engines of type PT6A-34 with quiet four-blade propellers.
aircraft.care: We ask you to help take care of JMP. Treat The White Swan with care and love!

insurance.title: Insurance for
insurance.norwegianText: Are covered through NLF and do not need additional insurance.
insurance.foreignIntro: You must have valid third-party liability insurance.
insurance.foreignBuy: If you cannot document this, you can buy NLF's insurance for 503 NOK (30 days) through the club.
insurance.foreignWarning: For jumpers from countries outside EU/EEA, we strongly recommend having travel insurance that covers medical treatment in Norway.

reporting.title: Reporting
reporting.intro: We want Tønsberg Fallskjermklubb to be a safe sports arena for all our members, students and visitors. This includes safety during jumping activities and in social settings.
reporting.policy: In Norwegian sports, everyone should be safe. There is zero tolerance for discrimination, bullying and harassment. By reporting, you give us the opportunity to handle critical conditions.
reporting.systemDesc: We use MittVarsel, a digital portal for safe and secure reporting. You can report with your name or anonymously.
reporting.group: Reporting group: Leader: Odd Pedersen. Members: Anna Fasting and Silje Søraas.

q1.question: How do I renew my membership?
q1.answer: Go to nlf.no/grener/fallskjerm/Medlem/minidrett/ to renew membership, insurance and license.

q2.question: I haven't jumped in a while, what do I need to do?
q2.answer: It depends on which license you had when you last jumped, and how long it's been. See table in Handbook part 300, parachute licenses.

q3.question: What are the currency requirements for my license?
q3.answer: A-license: 20 jumps last year. B-license: 20 jumps last year. C-license: 40 jumps last year. D-license: 40 jumps last year. See Handbook part 300 for all details.

q4.question: Can I deposit money to my Burble account online?
q4.answer: No, not yet. You must deposit money at reception (debit card or cash), or transfer to our account 1594.16.71664.

q5.question: What about insurance for foreign jumpers?
q5.answer: Norwegian jumpers are covered through NLF. Foreign jumpers must have valid third-party liability insurance. Without documentation, you can buy NLF's insurance for 503 NOK (30 days). For jumpers from outside EU/EEA, we strongly recommend travel insurance that covers medical treatment in Norway.

q6.question: What are the rules for tracking and wingsuit?
q6.answer: Max 3 horizontal groups per load: Max 2 Angle (tracking) + Max 1 WS/Tracksuit. Check Jumper Manifest Display before manifesting. If you need to track when there are already two groups, you must coordinate or do something else. Use 'Angle' under Formation, not 'Tracking'.

q7.question: I'm having trouble with Min Idrett. What can I do?
q7.answer: See tips from NLF on their website. Remember that it's now called 'kompetansebevis' and not 'lisens' or 'sertifikat'. The word 'lisens' in MinIdrett means 'insurance'.

q8.question: Where can I find the JLS Operations Manual?
q8.answer: The Operations Manual can be found at jarlsbergluftsportssenter.no. When you register at Skydive Tønsberg, you must sign that you have familiarized yourself with it.

faq.title: Frequently asked
faq.description: Here you'll find answers to the most common questions we get. Don't hesitate to contact us if you have other questions!

q1.question: What is the age limit for tandem jumping?
q1.answer: You must be 18 years old to jump tandem. If you're between 16 and 18, you need written consent from both parents. If you're over 80, you need an approved medical certificate.

q2.question: How high do we jump from?
q2.answer: We jump from 4000 meters! This gives you about 40 seconds of freefall at around 200 km/h before the tandem instructor deploys the parachute at 1500 meters. During the 5-minute canopy ride, you can enjoy the view over the Oslo Fjord and Tønsberg archipelago.

q3.question: What is the maximum weight for tandem jumping?
q3.answer: Maximum weight is 110 kg. In some cases we can allow slightly over 100 kg, but this depends on your physical condition and is assessed by the instructor in each case.

q4.question: What happens if the weather is bad?
q4.answer: We don't jump when it's raining, too windy (more than 11 m/s ground wind), or if the cloud cover is low or dense. If we have to cancel due to weather, we'll notify you by SMS the same day. You can then book a new time free of charge, or get a refund for everything except the deposit.

q5.question: How long does a tandem jump take?
q5.answer: From arrival to jump completion usually takes 1-3 hours. This includes video briefing, form filling, gear fitting and briefing with your tandem instructor. Add some extra time as weather and wind can affect the schedule.

q6.question: Can I bring my own camera?
q6.answer: For safety reasons, it's not allowed to bring your own camera during the jump. We recommend ordering video and photos when you book – you'll most likely only do this once in your life, so it's nice to have good memories!

q7.question: How much does a tandem jump cost?
q7.answer: Tandem jumps cost 4690 NOK on weekdays and 5190 NOK on weekends. Prices include all fees, membership and insurance. Video costs 800 NOK, video and photos 1290 NOK, and full video package with dedicated camera person costs 1780 NOK.

q8.question: How can I become an independent skydiver?
q8.answer: Take our AFF basic course (Accelerated Freefall)! The course includes 10 hours ground school, 10 min wind tunnel at Gardermoen, and 7 jumps with instructors. After the course (Level 1-7) you do 13 solo jumps before you can get your A-license. Complete course costs 18,990 NOK.

q9.question: How long is the gift certificate valid?
q9.answer: Gift certificates are valid for 12 months from purchase date. You can pass it on to others if you don't use it yourself.

q10.question: Can I jump together with friends or family?
q10.answer: Yes! You'll be on the same aircraft, up to 4 at once, and jump out with about 10 seconds between each. You'll land in the same area shortly after each other. If you have a friend who's a skydiver, they can also jump with you if the tandem instructor approves it.

q1.question: The jump is a surprise – what do I do?
q1.answer: When booking for others as a surprise, provide YOUR email and YOUR mobile number – then we'll only communicate with you. Our rules state that the jumper must be notified at least 48 hours before the jump.

q2.question: The weather forecast is bad, will there be jumping?
q2.answer: We don't jump when it's raining, too windy (more than 11 m/s), or if the cloud cover is low or dense. If we must cancel, we'll notify you by SMS the same day. If you don't hear from us, just come!

q3.question: I weigh over 100 kg, can I jump?
q3.answer: In some cases we allow over 100 kg, but it depends on your physical condition/fitness and is assessed by the instructor in each case. Maximum limit is 110 kg. Weather and wind conditions also play a role.

q4.question: Can I jump together with others?
q4.answer: Yes! You'll be on the same aircraft, up to 4 at once, and jump out with about 10 seconds between each. You'll land in the same place shortly after each other. If you have a friend who's a skydiver, they can jump with you if the instructor approves it.

q5.question: What happens if my jump is cancelled?
q5.answer: If we must cancel due to weather or other reasons, we'll book you for a new time free of charge. Or we'll refund what you paid, except the deposit. Up to you!

q6.question: How long is the gift certificate valid?
q6.answer: The gift certificate is valid for 12 months from purchase date. You can pass it on to others if you don't use it yourself.

q7.question: I haven't received the video link from my jump!
q7.answer: Check your spam filter. Sender is skydive-tonsberg.wetransfer.com. You can also search for 'wetransfer' on your PC. Still can't find it – contact us!

q8.question: How far in advance should I book?
q8.answer: High season is from May to end of October. Popular times fill up quickly, especially Saturdays and Sundays. Book as early as possible to secure your preferred time. Weekdays have more availability.

q1.question: What does a rejump cost if I don't pass a level?
q1.answer: The 7 jumps in the course each have their own skill requirements. If you fail a level, you must redo it. Rejumps with instructors are paid in addition to the course price. See price list at the dropzone.

q2.question: What happens after the course (Level 1-7)?
q2.answer: After the course you're a Level 8 student. You must do 13 Level 8 jumps alone, including 2 FS checkouts and 2 low jumps with instructor. Then you can get your A-license through written exam, packing course and A-course.

q3.question: How dangerous is skydiving?
q3.answer: There's always a risk with skydiving. But if you do as you're told and instructed, you're safe. If your main parachute doesn't work as it should, you get rid of it and deploy the reserve. You also have an AAD that opens the reserve automatically at a certain altitude.

q4.question: What if I don't dare to jump?
q4.answer: If you're already in the aircraft, you'll come down with it again. You still have to pay for the instructors and your own seat in the aircraft.

q5.question: How far in advance should I sign up?
q5.answer: The first courses fill up first. Sign up as soon as you've found a course with dates that suit you! We run 13 courses in the season from late April to mid-October.

q6.question: What do I need to bring to the course?
q6.answer: Bring workout clothes, sneakers, warm clothes (especially spring and fall), something to take notes on, and a good mood! Wool sweater as base layer is smart, and some days you'll need tights or long underwear under the jumpsuit.
